subject.title: fix(acpx): drain leased descendants when turns are aborted

question: Should OpenClaw preserve the upstream cancel/close distinction with an explicit terminate-and-drain path, or intentionally make every shared ACP cancel close and evict the live runtime and allow unresolved stale containment to block ACPX startup?
rationale: The dependency already exposes separate lifecycle operations, four OpenClaw caller families have different intent, and the fail-closed startup behavior changes compatibility and availability in a way tests cannot authorize.

options.title: Separate cancel from containment
options.body: Preserve cooperative cancel for reusable sessions and route abort, reset, and task teardown through explicit close-and-drain behavior with visible operator recovery.

options.title: Approve the global override
options.body: Accept close-and-evict semantics for every cancel caller and manual recovery from fail-closed ACPX startup as the supported contract.

options.title: Pause for upstream lifecycle design
options.body: Hold the PR until ACPX owns or exposes the reusable containment operation and recovery contract.

recommendation.title: Separate cancel from containment
recommendation.body: Preserve cooperative cancel for reusable sessions and route abort, reset, and task teardown through explicit close-and-drain behavior with visible operator recovery.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced both the ACPX lifecycle hardening and the focused ACP manager cancellation module, making him the strongest history-backed owner for this contract decision.
